protocol: Six alternating AB/BA pairs per compiler runtime. Same full CLI source, cli_main entry, RC output. Fresh cache per pair and variant, cold then warm in separate processes. Equal-length compiler/cache/output paths. Production module caches enabled; checked-module, AST, and codegen-body caches disabled. Node wrapper with exnref and stack-size=4000. No CPU profiler in timing runs. heap_ptr is allocator high-water; RSS is the process reading at completion, not peak RSS.

import hashlib, json, os, pathlib, re, statistics, subprocess, time

root = pathlib.Path.cwd()
work = root / '_build/typeenv2387/compare'
assert work.is_dir()
env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith(('VIBE_', 'NODE_'))}
env.update(VIBE_PREOPEN_DIR=str(root), VIBE_IMPORT_ABI='raw', VIBE_WASM_MEMORY_STATS='1', VIBE_FS_COMPILE='1', VIBE_BACKEND='wasi', VIBE_RC='1', VIBE_CHECKED_MODULE_CACHE='off', VIBE_EXPERIMENTAL_AST_CACHE='0', VIBE_CODEGEN_BODY_CACHE='off', VIBE_WASM_NAMES='0')
report = json.loads((work / 'results.json').read_text())
assert len(report['runs']) == 24
report['protocol'] = report['protocol'].replace('Three alternating', 'Six alternating')
expected = report['runs'][0]['output_sha256']
for runtime in ['bump', 'rc']:
    for iteration in range(3, 6):
        for side in ('ab' if iteration % 2 == 0 else 'ba'):
            folder = work / f'{runtime}-{iteration}-{side}'
            folder.mkdir()
            for temperature in ['cold', 'warm']:
                out = folder / 'out.wasm'
                out.unlink(missing_ok=True)
                start = time.monotonic()
                proc = subprocess.run(['bash', 'scripts/run_wasm_vibe_host_runner.sh', '--invoke', 'cli_main', str(work / f'{side}-{runtime}.wasm'), 'lib/@vibe/cli/entry.vibe', str(out), 'cli_main'], env={**env, 'VIBE_BUILD_CACHE_DIR': str(folder / 'cache')}, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
                wall = time.monotonic() - start
                (folder / f'{temperature}.log').write_text(proc.stdout + proc.stderr)
                proc.check_returncode()
                digest = hashlib.sha256(out.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
                if expected is not None:
                    assert digest == expected, (runtime, side, temperature, digest, expected)
                expected = digest
                stats = re.findall(r'\[wasm-memory\][^\n]+', proc.stderr)[-1]
                row = {'runtime': runtime, 'round': iteration, 'variant': side, 'temperature': temperature, 'wall_s': wall, 'output_sha256': digest, 'output_bytes': out.stat().st_size, **{k: int(v) for k, v in re.findall(r'(pages|bytes|heap_ptr|rss)=([0-9]+)', stats)}}
                report['runs'].append(row)
                (work / 'results.json').write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + '\n')
                print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
report['medians'] = []
for runtime in ['bump', 'rc']:
    for temperature in ['cold', 'warm']:
        row = {'runtime': runtime, 'temperature': temperature}
        for side in 'ab':
            rs = [r for r in report['runs'] if (r['runtime'], r['temperature'], r['variant']) == (runtime, temperature, side)]
            row[side] = {k: statistics.median(r[k] for r in rs) for k in ['wall_s', 'heap_ptr', 'pages', 'rss']}
        row['delta_percent'] = {k: (row['b'][k] / row['a'][k] - 1) * 100 for k in row['a']}
        report['medians'].append(row)
        print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
report['extension_harness'] = pathlib.Path(__file__).read_text()
(work / 'results.json').write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + '\n')
print('DONE', flush=True)
title: Immutable TypeEnv name-to-row indexes: bounded symbol lookup trial
scope: EnvCached owns an opaque immutable EnvNameIndex: a copied name array in canonical transport order and an open-addressed name-to-binding-row table.

Row IDs are local to one cached node. Duplicate rows remain in transport order, and lookup returns the first row. EnvBind and AST identifiers still carry strings; this is not a compiler-wide symbol pool.
Cache misses continue through rest. Non-shadowing binds stay behind the cached node; shadowing binds precede it. Rebuilds ignore stale cached rows and read the authoritative chain.
Malformed name ordering remains available to artifact validators; its lookup keeps the previous binary-search behavior. Sorted rows are the lookup precondition.
Disk TypeEnv v9/v10 and checked-program v1 formats still encode names. Decoding rebuilds the index. Golden bytes captured from the baseline pin compatibility.
interpretation: Treat this as an encapsulation and representation change, not a demonstrated whole-build speedup. The private index can change without changing TypeEnv consumers or transport bytes.

All 48 uninstrumented timing outputs and 12 CPU-profile outputs are byte-identical. The allocator high-water increase is deterministic: +3,700,664 bytes bump cold, +2,237,416 bytes RC cold, +3,384/+3,256 bytes warm. Linear-memory pages are unchanged.

Wall measurements are variable. Bump cold changes sign between mean and median; initial N=3 and final N=6 differ substantially on RC. Keep all runs and both statistics; do not attribute the large pooled RC wall reduction to a roughly 10 ms lookup difference.
Cold CPU profiles (N=3) move lookup-inclusive medians from 245.166 to 239.336 ms bump and 547.339 to 537.415 ms RC. This small difference does not establish a net speedup after index construction.
V8 can inline the index and binary-search helpers. Zero samples for an individual helper mean no separately visible frame, not zero work.
A next experiment should measure the EnvBind chain and the cost of maintaining IDs through name resolution before extending the representation further.
timing_batches: Rounds 0-2, then the separate cold CPU-profile series, then rounds 3-5. Each timing pair alternates AB/BA; six rounds balance both orders. No local builds or tests ran concurrently with measurements. All fresh-cache cold/warm pairs use separate compiler processes and retain the same production cache settings.

cpu_profiles.protocol: Three alternating AB/BA cold profiles per runtime, fresh cache for every profile. Separate from uninstrumented timing runs. Same CLI source, RC output, flags and compiler artifacts as compare.py.
